title: Greek Chickpea Salad
instructions: Add the chickpeas, cucumber, tomatoes, red onion, and olives to a large bowl.
Whisk together the olive oil, red wine vinegar, oregano, salt, and pepper in a small bowl.
Pour the dressing over the salad and toss gently to combine.
Scatter the feta cubes on top and give it one more light toss.
Let it sit for 5 minutes before serving so the flavors mingle.

title: French Onion Soup
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onions and sugar, and cook low and slow, stirring occasionally, for 35-40 minutes until deep golden brown.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute, then pour in the wine, scraping up any browned bits.
Add the beef stock, thyme, and bay leaf, then simmer uncovered for 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Ladle the soup into oven-safe bowls, top each with a toasted baguette slice and a generous handful of Gruyère.
Broil for 2-3 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and golden, then serve immediately.

title: Vietnamese Beef Pho
ingredients: Bean sprouts, Thai basil, lime wedges, and sliced chili to serve
instructions: Char the onion and ginger halves directly over a flame or under a hot broiler until blackened in spots, then rinse off any loose char.
Toast the star anise, cinnamon, and cloves in a dry pot over medium heat for 1-2 minutes until fragrant.
Add the beef stock, charred onion, and ginger, then simmer uncovered for 45 minutes.
Stir in the fish sauce and sugar, then strain the broth to remove the solids and keep it at a gentle simmer.
Cook the rice noodles according to the package instructions and divide them between bowls.
Lay the raw sliced beef over the hot noodles, then ladle the boiling broth on top so it cooks the beef instantly.
Serve with bean sprouts, Thai basil, lime wedges, and chili on the side.

title: Lemon Garlic Shrimp Scampi
instructions: Cook the linguine in salted boiling water until al dente, then reserve 1/2 cup of the pasta water and drain.
Heat the olive oil and half the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Season the shrimp with salt and pepper, then cook for 1-2 minutes per side until just pink. Remove and set aside.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes to the same skillet and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the wine and simmer for 2 minutes, then stir in the lemon juice and remaining butter.
Return the shrimp and drained linguine to the skillet, tossing with a splash of the reserved pasta water until glossy.
Finish with the chopped parsley and serve immediately.

title: Chocolate Lava Cake
ingredients: 2 tbsp all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting
Powdered sugar and vanilla ice cream, to serve
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220°C (425°F) and butter and flour four ramekins.
Melt the chocolate and butter together in a heatproof bowl set over simmering water, then let cool slightly.
Whisk the eggs, egg yolks, and sugar together until pale and slightly thickened.
Fold the melted chocolate into the egg mixture, then gently fold in the flour and salt until just combined.
Divide the batter between the ramekins and bake for 10-12 minutes until the sides are set but the center still jiggles slightly.
Let the cakes rest for 1 minute, then invert onto plates, dust with powdered sugar, and serve with a scoop of ice cream.

title: Thai Green Curry
instructions: Scoop the thick cream from the top of one coconut milk can into a wok or large pan and heat until it starts to split and sizzle.
Add the green curry paste and fry for 2-3 minutes until very fragrant.
Add the chicken and cook for 3-4 minutes until lightly seared on the outside.
Pour in the remaining coconut milk, then add the eggplant, bell pepper, green beans, and kaffir lime leaves.
Simmer for 15-18 minutes until the chicken is cooked through and the vegetables are tender.
Stir in the fish sauce and brown sugar, then taste and adjust seasoning.
Scatter with Thai basil and serve hot over jasmine rice.

title: Crispy Falafel Wrap
ingredients: 1 can chickpeas, drained and patted dry
Shredded lettuce, sliced tomato, and pickled onions, to serve
instructions: Pulse the chickpeas, onion, garlic, parsley, cumin, and coriander in a food processor until finely chopped but not pureed.
Add the flour and baking powder and pulse a few more times until the mixture holds together when pressed.
Shape the mixture into small patties or balls.
Heat about 2cm of oil in a skillet over medium heat and fry the falafel in batches for 2-3 minutes per side until golden and crisp.
Drain the falafel on paper towels.
Spread hummus over each flatbread, then fill with lettuce, tomato, pickled onions, and the warm falafel before rolling up.

title: Quinoa Buddha Bowl
note: colorful, nourishing, no cooking skill required
instructions: Combine the quinoa and stock in a saucepan, bring to a boil, then cover and simmer for 15 minutes until the liquid is absorbed. Fluff with a fork and let cool slightly.
Whisk together the tahini, lemon juice, soy sauce, maple syrup, and a splash of water until smooth and pourable.
Divide the quinoa between bowls and arrange the cabbage, carrot, avocado, tomatoes, and edamame on top in sections.
Drizzle generously with the tahini dressing and sprinkle with sesame seeds before serving.
